issues.where: Stuck-at campaign, worker lanes W1–W6 (bottom centre)
issues.problem: The progress bars never move. At 2 s, 18 s and 34 s, W1–W5 all read exactly 3840 and W6 reads exactly 2944, even though the batch numbers advance (#176 → #266 → #356). The display seems to refresh only when a batch ends. At 49 s it swings the other way: W1–W5 show 0, 0/31 and empty bitmaps while W6 sits at 3200. In both cases the panel looks frozen or idle.
issues.fix: Post per-worker cycle progress from the fault workers every ~100 ms, not only at batch end. Start each worker's batch at a different offset so the six bars are never all full or all empty together. When a batch finishes, keep its bitmap showing (dimmed) until the next batch has detections.

issues.where: Die floorplan, top centre (18 s frame)
issues.problem: When the probe moves to n12072 at site (106,13), its tooltip covers the gold 'critical path 49 levels · fwdA > Baugh-Wooley…' label, so the hero panel shows two labels stacked on top of each other.
issues.fix: Collision-test the probe tooltip against the fixed labels (stage boxes, fwd brackets, critical-path tag) and flip it below or left of the probe point. Or pin the probe readout to a fixed corner of the floorplan and draw a leader line to the cell.

issues.where: Top bar vs controls vs netlist hierarchy vs floorplan header
issues.problem: One quantity shows three different values at the same moment. At 2 s, est. power reads 0.517 mW (floorplan), 0.539 mW (controls) and 533.2 µW (core row). Toggles/cycle reads 2,129 (floorplan), 2,194 (core TOG/C) and 3,607 (analyzer), and α reads 15.2% vs 15.7%. Each value is probably correct for its own averaging window, but the windows are not labelled, so the numbers look inconsistent.
issues.fix: Either feed all three from one EMA, or label the window on each (e.g. 'α 15.2% · last 256 cyc', 'avg 1 s', 'this cycle').

issues.where: Pipeline trace and retired list (right dock) vs top bar
issues.problem: The retired list says '1,003,820 checked' and shows cycles 1053195–1053199, but the top bar and golden badge already say instret 1,004,203 at cycle 1,053,600. The trace runs one chunk (~400 cycles) behind the counters.
issues.fix: Snapshot the counters and the trace from the same chunk, or show the trace's own cycle in its header so the lag reads as intentional.

issues.where: Logic analyzer time axis and pipeline column headers
issues.problem: The cycle labels are truncated mod 100000 ('51723', '19959', '53184') while every other place shows full cycle numbers (1,051,939). They read as unrelated numbers.
issues.fix: Show the full cycle number at the left edge (e.g. '1,051,723') and an offset after it ('+20', '+40'), or prefix the truncated labels with '…'.

issues.where: Die floorplan, bottom module-label row and CTL strip (y≈680–760)
issues.problem: The gold critical-path line runs through the 'fwd' module label, and the 'write-back …' and 'pc redirect …' tags sit right on the label row. The CTL strip below is mostly empty dark space with a few sparse columns.
issues.fix: Stop the critical-path polyline at the die edge, or route it above the label row. Move the write-back and redirect tags into the CTL strip so that space carries information.

issues.problem: It shows 'occupancy · last 16 cycles', but the brief asks for 24 cycles.
issues.fix: Widen to 24 cycles (shrink the cells by about 2 px), or update the brief or notes.

issues.problem: Threads are labelled only T00–T15. The brief asks for labels showing which worker (sim, fault W1–W6, render) runs on each thread.
issues.fix: Add a small worker tag next to each Txx label (e.g. 'T04 · W3'), taken from the worker-to-thread assignment, or mark 'sim' on the busiest thread.

issues.where: Framebuffer, current frame below the write cursor
issues.problem: The rows not yet painted show a dimmed copy of the previous frame. At 34 s and 49 s this looks like a smeared second image, a rendering glitch rather than stale RAM.
issues.fix: Draw the unpainted rows as a faint grid or a dark hatch, or label them 'stale f2'.

issues.problem: Frame JS averages 4.39 ms but peaks at 220 ms. A spike like that during recording drops about 13 frames and shows as a visible hitch.
issues.fix: Make sure the spike (probably netlist compile or the first WebGL upload) happens before the 30 s recorder warmup ends. Spread any per-frame-boundary work, such as the per-row UART or thumbnail rebuild, across several frames.

critic.summary:
This is very strong, and the numbers hold up when you check them against each other. 12,440 gates × 24 kHz gives exactly 298.6 M gate evals/s. 1/IPC matches CPI. The hierarchy rows add up (pp 1024 + dadda 4559 + ks64 1052 = mul 6635). The critical-path segments sum to 49. Frame, row and pixel numbers agree between the top bar, the framebuffer and the UART (48·17+5 = 821). 444 batches × 31 faults = 13,764 sampled, and 11,311 / 13,764 = 82.2%. The power figure matches ½·tog·C·V²·f. The pipeline stage labels show a correct BTFN redirect bubble and an IF flush.

The EDA-editor layout fits the subject, the grid is tight, the hierarchy is datasheet-dense, and the Dadda-tree triangle is a striking centrepiece. The recording clearly opens mid-run, with frame 1 finished and frame 2 painting.

Two problems are visible at a glance. The fault campaign's worker lanes look frozen in three frames and nearly empty in the fourth. In the 18 s frame, the probe tooltip covers the critical-path label in the hero panel. The rest is small consistency polish: averaging windows that aren't labelled, a trace running one chunk behind the counters, and truncated cycle labels.

For wow, the Mandelbrot payoff is small, and its ×2 zoom at MAXIT 32 fills more of each frame with black. Even so, the density and the clear signs of real simulation should stop people scrolling. Fix the two major issues and this can be posted.
